Never write the name of the reference product, nor a path of this computer, into a Sai file or a handoff (write <scratch> or <outside the project>). findings.what: PLT-04 forbids the word `import` anywhere in the source text of tools/src/platform-guard.js, but the design does not say that comments count, and the design's own sketch module carries the comment «Pure: no import, no environment, no disk.», so PLT-04 as designed is red on the sketch (measured; with the comment reworded to «loads no module», as node-floor.js words it, PLT-04 is green and U8 variants are red).
findings.needed: Section 2 (and PLT-04) say that the whole text, comments included, holds none of the banned words (as PE-8b of the picker states «comments count»), so BACKEND-DEV/CODE-FIXER do not copy the sketch comment.

findings.what: T1 says a platform guard added to traces/cli.js (or the other help-only thin-client tools) is caught by «PLT-10 (that row), PLT-11». Measured: a guard placed after the help branch of traces/cli.js leaves every PLT-10 row green (traces, handoffs-check, handoff and picker are probed only by --help, answered before the floor guard); only PLT-11's word grep catches it, and a guard written without the module name would pass both.
findings.needed: Either the T1 row names PLT-11 as the catcher for the help-only tools, or PLT-10 adds one non-help call of traces (and handoffs-check/handoff) that passes the floor guard and writes nothing in the test folder.
